newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends limit down in line with CBOT soy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends limit down in line with CBOT soy.

text.p: WCE canola closed locked the $10.00-limit down in tandem with a skid in CBOT soybeans, traders said. November canola ended at $410.70 a tonne.
CBOT soybeans tumbled on an increase in the U.S. Department of Agriculture's U.S. soybean production estimate to 2.346 billion bushels from 2.270 billion, traders said.

Other bearish factors included forecasts for favorable harvest weather for the next few days and news that Cargill Ltd, a unit of U.S.-based Cargill Inc was temporarily shutting down its canola crushing operations at Clavet, Saskatchewan by the end of the month.
Also, CanAmera Foods said it would cut its canola crush in Canada by "20 percent or more" in late November due to poor crush margins.
"It was the USDA report," one trader said of the futures slide. "Crush margins are (also) terrible, so naturally plants are backing off from their buying."
October flax dropped $7.50 at $391.00. "Crushers were aggressive buyers for flaxseed which kept the price from going limit down," the trader said.
Western barley posted new contract lows in all contracts except for spot November which fell $3.30 at $142.70.
The selling spilled over into feed wheat which also set new contract lows from December to July positions. October feed wheat dropped $3.50 to $170.50.
(All values in Canadian dollars except for feed peas and oats which are in U.S. dollars).
